content: This interaction necessitates the use of alternative therapies. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of ivosidenib, ixabepilone, ixazomib, ketoconazole, lapatinib, larotrectinib, ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, lefamulin, lemborexant, lenacapavir, leniolisib, levamlodipine, levoketoconazole, levonorgestrel (oral and intrauterine), linagliptin, lofepramine, lomitapide, lonafarnib, lopinavir, loratadine, lorlatinib, losartan, lovastatin, lumacaftor/ivacaftor, lumateperone, lumefantrine, lurasidone, lurbinectedin, macimorelin, macitentan, maprotiline, maraviroc, mavacamten, medroxyprogesterone, mefloquine, mestranol, methadone, methylprednisolone, metoprolol, miconazole (vaginal), midazolam, midostaurin, mifepristone, mirtazapine, mitotane, modafinil, montelukast, morphine, naloxegol, naldemedine, nelfinavir, neratinib, netupitant/palonosetron, nevirapine, nicardipine, nifedipine, nilotinib, nimodipine, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, nisoldipine, nitrendipine, norethindrone (oral, acetate, and transdermal), norgestrel, nortriptyline, olaparib, oliceridine, olutasidenib, omaveloxolone, ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir, ondansetron, osilodrostat, osimertinib, ospemifene, oxazepam, oxybutynin, oxycodone, paclitaxel, pacritinib, palbociclib, palovarotene, panobinostat, parecoxib, paricalcitol, pazopanib, pemigatinib, perampanel, pexidartinib, phenindione, phenobarbital, phenytoin, pimavanserin, pimozide, pioglitazone, pirtobrutinib, and other drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. In most cases, rifabutin induces hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes, leading to increased metabolism and reduced efficacy of the affected drugs. This interaction often requires avoiding co-administration, using alternative therapies, or closely monitoring the patient for therapeutic efficacy and adverse effects. For some drugs, dose adjustments may be necessary to maintain therapeutic levels. Hormonal contraceptives, when co-administered with rifabutin, may become unreliable, necessitating the use of alternative or backup contraceptive methods. For drugs like larotrectinib, doubling the dose may be required if co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable. Similarly, for drugs like macimorelin, discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inducer with sufficient washout time is recommended before testing. In cases involving ritonavir, rifabutin doses should be reduced by at least 75% to minimize adverse effects such as neutropenia and uveitis. Certain drugs, such as ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, lonafarnib, naloxegol, lorlatinib, lumefantrine, and panobinostat, are contraindicated with rifabutin due to the risk of significant therapeutic failure or adverse effects. For others, such as palbociclib and olutasidenib, strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce plasma concentrations by up to 85%, necessitating alternative treatments.
